documents.sources/aestivation/README.md: Plans, verdicts, and the assembly gate # aestivation Plan proposal, deterministic validation, review verdicts, and the assembly gate. Aestivation is the admission and review member of the bloom agent family. Before work opens, it happens here: a plan is proposed, a deterministic rule pack validates it, reviewers record approve or revise verdicts, and a gate holds automatic assembly until the plan is both valid and approved. A revision verdict stops assembly; the reasons say what to change; the next plan is a new proposal. ## Status Version 0.5.0. The plan rule pack, verdict ledger, and assembly gate are `implemented` as a tested reference library. A durable ledger, live reviewers, and service interfaces remain `specified` or `planned`. ## Install ```bash npm install @vidoxlabs/aestivation ``` Requires Node >= 22.13. Zero runtime dependencies. ## Modules | Module | What it holds | Label | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `plan.mjs` | Plan proposals: objective plus ordered steps, the SHA-256 digest of each proposal's content, and the deterministic rule pack that validates stages, titles, and order. | `implemented` | | `verdict.mjs` | Verdict records (approve or revise) that may name the plan digest they reviewed, the append-only ledger, and the soundness check over every record. | `implemented` | | `intent.mjs` | Read-only intent assessments that name missing sources and ground personal recall in admitted memory references. Tool and memory-write lists stay under caller admission. | `implemented` | | `correction.mjs` | Corrections within existing scope after an exact-digest revise verdict, with new frozen proposals, a two-replan limit per in-process lineage, and a check that refuses superseded results. The judge cannot apply the patch. | `implemented` | | `gate.mjs` | The assembly gate: one function that checks the ledger, holds a review of a different plan version as stale, and composes validation and verdicts into permitted or held, with the reason. | `implemented` | ## The name Aestivation is the arrangement of petals in a bud before it opens. That is the entire doctrine: the work of arranging before the opening. Nothing assembles until the arrangement has been validated and reviewed. When it opens, it opens because the gate said so for stated reasons. ## The rule pack The baseline deterministic rules a plan must pass: 1. A plan has at least one step. 2. Every step names a known stage: `research`, `work`, `review`, `assemble`, or `verify`. 3. Every step has a non-empty title. 4. When review and assemble are both present, review precedes the first assemble. 5. When verify is present, it is the final step. The same plan validates the same way every time, and no review can wave it through. The split runs both ways: no rule pack approves a plan on a reviewer's behalf. Judgment and rules are separate lanes; the gate composes them. ## The family The family follows one design law: ordinary botanical words for public products, mirroring five flower-named personas. | Name | Province | | :--- | :--- | | [`seed`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) | Harness foundation: runs, tools, providers | | [`capillary`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary) | Context retrieval and relations, provenance-first | | [`myosotis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/myosotis) | Memory with consent and structural forget | | `aestivation` (this repo) | Plans, verdicts, and the gate before assembly | | [`drosera`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/drosera) | Tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks | | [`trellis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/trellis) | Multi-point testing with dated evidence | | [`bloom`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) | The team workspace harness | | [`docs`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs) | Family documentation, synced from every public repository | ## Documentation - `AGENTS.md`: start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province. - `docs/charter.md`: mission, principles, non-goals. - `docs/architecture.md`: the bud and its four whorls. - `docs/contracts/`: the plan, verdict, and gate contracts. - `docs/interop.md`: how bloom runs the loop, and how seed carries its effects. ## Development ```bash npm test ``` Tests use the Node built-in runner. Adding a rule means adding the test that holds it. ## License MIT The Vidoxlabs name and mark are trademarks of Vidoxlabs LLC. They are not covered by this repository's MIT license.
documents.sources/capillary/README.md: Context with its sources attached # Capillary Capillary is an open, local-first **context retrieval system** for agent workspaces. It records sources with their digests, retrieves **bounded, provenance-honest packets** of them, and keeps **typed relations** between the items it holds: the fine-channel work of lifting context up to the team that needs it, without letting prose smuggle in as fact. Agent surfaces like [Bloom](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) consume capillary exactly where retrieving (and organizing) their source and context matters: a team brief admits sources, and specialists receive bounded excerpts that say what they are, where they came from, and what was shortened. Harness foundations like [Seed](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) admit capillary's retrieval tools to their runs and record each retrieval as an intent. **Status: `1.3.0`, retrieval contracts and library modules.** The retrieval seam, source recording, and relation contracts are implemented and covered by `npm test`. The backing stores (index, service) are specified, not shipped. Nothing in this repository opens a network listener or retrieves over the network today. ## What is here today (`implemented`) | Module | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/provenance.mjs` | Records source digests, origins, evidence classes and confidence, and records why sources are unknown | | `src/packet.mjs` | Builds bounded context packets with **declared** truncation, budgeted admission, declared unknown sources, and relevance and recency kept as separate fields | | `src/epoch-guard.mjs` | Refuses a packet when the deletion epoch at the end of a read differs from the epoch at its start, or cannot be read | | `src/read.mjs` | Reads caller-supplied text under an estimated token budget and declares truncation in an untrusted envelope | | `src/search.mjs` | Searches caller-supplied records for literal matches and reports recency and snippet cuts in an untrusted envelope | | `src/conversation.mjs` | Shapes one conversation's thread, a recent list, a brief of the newest operator intent and verified outcome, and an envelope around the parent walk, all from caller-supplied records | | `src/relations.mjs` | Typed, append-only relations and bounded walks over supplied parent links | `npm install && npm test` verifies all of it. No runtime dependencies. ## Contracts - [Bounded retrieval](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): the packet, its budgets, declared shortening, declared omissions - [Provenance](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): digests and origin classes on every source ## How capillary fits the family (`specified`) The botanic line, per [docs/family.md](docs/family.md): **seed** (the foundation a runtime grows from) → **capillary** (these channels, lifting context to it) → **myosotis** (governed memory: consent, keep, and forget) → **aestivation** (the bud's arrangement, admission and review before assembly) → **drosera** (the sundew's tentacles: tools, skills, hooks, cookbooks) → **bloom** (the opened team workspace), with the whole line growing against **trellis** (the testing lattice that keeps every member honest). Capillary owns retrieval and organization only. Remembering with consent is the memory fabric's job (forget is a promise there, not a default); deciding what gets admitted into runs and what assembles is the gate's job. [docs/interop.md](docs/interop.md) draws each seam. ## Documentation - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province. - [Charter](docs/charter.md): mission, principles, non-goals - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): sources, index, packets, relations - [Contracts](docs/contracts/retrieval.md): bounded retrieval and provenance - [Relations contract](docs/contracts/relations.md): typed, append-only context relations - [Interop](docs/interop.md): Bloom, Seed, and the memory seam - [Family](docs/family.md): the botanic naming line ## License [MIT](LICENSE) The Vidoxlabs name and mark are trademarks of Vidoxlabs LLC. They are not covered by this repository's MIT license.
documents.sources/drosera/README.md: Tools, skills, hooks, and cookbooks # drosera Tooling for agents: tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks. Drosera is the tooling member of the bloom agent family. It defines the four packaging forms an agent works with beyond its own context. Tool faces are neutral definitions of what can be called, following seed's tool-id grammar. Skills are packaged instructions that grow context without granting authority. Hooks are deterministic checks, fail closed, bound to run events. Cookbooks are recipes that compose published faces and skills, resolved at validation. ## The name Drosera is the sundew. A sundew works by extension: sticky tentacles that reach out from the plant and hold what they touch, each one honest about what it has caught. That is the doctrine here: tools reach, each face says what it grips (summary, effect class), and the extensions never become the organism. The harness is the organism; drosera is what it holds. ## Status Version 2.2.0. Pack formats, validation, reference resolution, the skill document reader, and the in-memory skill catalog are `implemented` in the reference library. A live registry, connector bindings, and server interfaces remain `specified` or `planned`. ## Install ```bash npm install @vidoxlabs/drosera ``` Requires Node >= 22.13. Zero runtime dependencies. ## Modules | Module | What it holds | Label | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `pack.mjs` | Tool faces under seed's neutral tool-id grammar, and the tool pack that collects them with unique IDs and domain listings. | `implemented` | | `skills.mjs` | Skill validation, lifecycle transitions, skill packs, and a catalog for promoted MIT skills. | `implemented` | | `skill-markdown.mjs` | Reads a skill document's text, which the caller already holds, into the record `skills.mjs` checks. It opens no file. | `implemented` | | `hooks.mjs` | Hook records: deterministic checks bound to run events, and the fail-closed hook pack. | `implemented` | | `cookbook.mjs` | Recipes composing faces and skills, with validation that every reference resolves. | `implemented` | ## The family The family follows one design law: ordinary botanical words for public products, mirroring five flower-named personas ([the law](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary/blob/main/docs/family.md)). | Name | Province | | :--- | :--- | | [`seed`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) | Harness foundation: runs, tools, providers | | [`capillary`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary) | Context retrieval and relations, provenance-first | | [`myosotis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/myosotis) | Memory with consent and structural forget | | [`aestivation`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/aestivation) | Plans, verdicts, and the gate before assembly | | `drosera` (this repo) | Tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks | | [`trellis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/trellis) | Multi-point testing with dated evidence | | [`bloom`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) | The team workspace harness | | [`docs`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs) | Family documentation, synced from every public repository | ## Documentation - `AGENTS.md`: start here before editing. documents.sources/myosotis/README.md: Memory that keeps only what you allow # myosotis Governed memory for agents: consent to keep, structural forget. Myosotis is the memory member of the bloom agent family. It holds the contracts and reference modules for agent memory where two promises sit on the face of the thing: memory is only kept under proper consent, and a real forget is structural. A forget invalidates every projection built before it and withholds forgotten content from later reads. A stale projection fails closed; it never resurrects. ## Status Version 1.2.0. The record, consent, forget, bounded recall, and in-process continuity rules are `implemented` as a tested reference library. A durable store, projection adapters, and service interfaces remain `specified` or `planned`. ## Install ```bash npm install @vidoxlabs/myosotis ``` Requires Node >= 22.13. Zero runtime dependencies. ## Modules | Module | What it holds | Label | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `records.mjs` | Memory record shape and the closed set of memory classes: organizational, personal-consented, active-thread, unconfirmed. | `implemented` | | `consent.mjs` | Consent grants and revocations, ordered by an optional sequence so a later grant is re-consent, and the state that answers whether a scope currently has consent. | `implemented` | | `forget.mjs` | The memory store state machine: admission and supersede, the confirmed and keyed forget that tombstones a whole supersede chain, the epoch, and stamped projections of identifiers and digests that are refused once stale and rebuilt before they serve. | `implemented` | | `recall.mjs` | Bounded selection from caller-held records, with sensitivity checks and candidate, eligible, and selected counts. | `implemented` | | `continuity.mjs` | One active continuity per subject, held in the process. Lookup never opens one, attach refuses any id that is not this subject's active id without saying why, and isolate opens a new active id. | `implemented` | ## Why the classes stay distinguishable The four memory classes never collapse into one bucket: - **organizational**: knowledge that belongs to a scope, like a team's working notes. Kept without personal consent because it is not about a person. - **personal-consented** requires a live grant for its scope, an admissible sensitivity, and provenance of the principal's explicit confirmation. - **active-thread**: working context for the conversation happening now. Ephemeral by nature, never promoted to durable silently. - **unconfirmed**: an observation that has not been established. Stays marked. Never presented as known. Conflating them is the failure mode this fabric exists to prevent. ## Why forget is an epoch A forget that only deletes a row leaves every cached copy of that row alive. Myosotis models forget as an epoch bump: every projection (a cache, an index, a summary) carries the epoch it was built at, and any projection whose stamp no longer matches fails closed. Reading it is refused until it is rebuilt from the store. Bypass and rebuild, never resurrect. ## The family The family follows one design law: ordinary botanical words for public products, mirroring five flower-named personas. | Name | Province | | :--- | :--- | | [`seed`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) | Harness foundation: runs, tools, providers | | [`capillary`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary) | Context retrieval and relations, provenance-first | | `myosotis` (this repo) | Memory with consent and structural forget | | [`aestivation`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/aestivation) | Plans, verdicts, and the gate before assembly | | [`drosera`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/drosera) | Tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks | | [`trellis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/trellis) | Multi-point testing with dated evidence | | [`bloom`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) | The team workspace harness | | [`docs`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs) | Family documentation, synced from every public repository | ## Documentation - `AGENTS.md`: start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province. - `docs/charter.md`: mission, principles, non-goals. - `docs/architecture.md`: the parts and how they compose. - `docs/contracts/`: the record, consent, and forget contracts. - `docs/interop.md`: how bloom consumes memory, and where capillary ends and myosotis begins. ## Development ```bash npm test ``` Tests use the Node built-in runner. Adding a rule means adding the test that holds it. ## License MIT The Vidoxlabs name and mark are trademarks of Vidoxlabs LLC. They are not covered by this repository's MIT license.
documents.sources/seed/README.md: Contracts and schemas for the runtime # Seed Seed is an open, local-first harness foundation for AI agents. It defines the contracts an agent runtime is built on: the run model, tool identity, and the provider adapter. Agent workspaces like [Bloom](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) can orchestrate model-backed workers, tools, and shared artifacts without depending on any single hosted service or third-party harness. **Status: `0.8.0`, specification and contract modules.** The contracts, grammar, and validators in this repository are implemented and covered by `npm test`. The runtime services on the roadmap are specified or planned, not shipped. Nothing in this repository opens a network listener, calls a hosted model, or touches your files today. ## Why Bloom proved the model-agnostic part: a notebook-shaped team workspace that treats any chat-completions-compatible service as one provider binding of several. The layer below the model is still rented: a third-party harness decides how tools are called, how runs are recovered, and how work proves itself. Seed takes that layer back as a small, open, inspectable foundation: - **One run model.** Work is an *objective* with *attempts*, recorded intents, and a verification receipt, not a loose prompt history. - **Neutral tool identity.** Tools are addressed by grammar, never by vendor, host, or product name, so adapters can be swapped without re-teaching agents. - **Provider-agnostic by contract.** Any inference service that can complete text can sit behind the same `generate` contract Bloom already speaks. ## What is here today (`implemented`) | Module | What it does | | --- | --- | | `src/tool-id.mjs` | Parse, format, and validate the neutral tool ID grammar; check registry entries, rollback postures, and cross-entry references | | `src/run-model.mjs` | Objective/attempt records, run statuses, legal transitions, and intent-time tool admission | | `src/resume.mjs` | Resume pending steps, report supplied failure classes, preview steps in a dry run, and manage in-process run leases | | `src/admission.mjs` | Fail-closed caller admission over a registry the caller holds | | `src/registry-documents.mjs` | Check agents and tools documents the caller already parsed: name a document not supplied, and report an agent that names an unknown tool | | `src/provider.mjs` | Validate provider adapters and normalize generation results | | `src/model-alias.mjs` | Resolve the alias a caller asks for to a backend model name from a table the caller holds, keeping the two names distinct and labeling deprecated aliases without swapping them | `npm install && npm test` verifies all of it. There are no runtime dependencies. ## Contracts (`specified`, `implemented` where modules cover them) - [Run model](docs/contracts/run-model.md): objectives, attempts, intents, receipts - [Tool identity](docs/contracts/tool-id.md): the neutral ID grammar and registry fields - [Provider adapter](docs/contracts/provider.md): the `generate` contract, compatible with Bloom's team provider ## How seed and Bloom fit (`specified`) Bloom already isolates its model layer behind one provider interface. Seed lands in three stages, each one usable by Bloom as it ships: 1. **Stage 1, library contracts.** Shared modules: tool IDs, run records, and provider validation (this release). 2. **Stage 2, inference endpoint.** A local service exposing an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions surface over any configured backend, which Bloom can consume today via its provider base URL. 3. **Stage 3, run engine and tool registry.** Durable objectives and attempts, an owner gate for effects that leave the run, and a tool registry adapters publish to. Details and worked examples: [docs/bloom-interop.md](docs/bloom-interop.md). ## Documentation - [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province. - [Charter](docs/charter.md): mission, principles, non-goals - [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): planes, authority, and what seed refuses to own - [Lexicon](docs/lexicon.md): how public repositories stay in generalized terms - [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md): staged, status-labeled ## Design principles 1. Local-first. A clean checkout runs; nothing phones home. 2. One authority per fact. Runs own run state; memory owns memory; tools own effects. 3. Receipts over vibes. A run completes with a verification receipt, not a self-report. 4. Effects are gated. Side effects that leave a run pause for the owner. 5. No vendor names in tool identity. Grammar first; connectors carry the brand. ## License [MIT](LICENSE) The Vidoxlabs name and mark are trademarks of Vidoxlabs LLC. They are not covered by this repository's MIT license.
documents.sources/trellis/README.md: Multi-point tests for the family # trellis Multi-point testing for the agent family: shape, behavior, consistency, operational. Trellis is the testing member of the bloom agent family. Every member repository keeps its own tests; trellis checks the family from the outside, from four points each: **shape** (the public surface is what it claims), **behavior** (the load-bearing invariants hold under direct calls), **consistency** (the siblings agree where they claim to, one grammar, shared conventions), and **operational** (each test suite runs green when actually run). Verdicts are pass, fail, or unknown. A fail always outranks an unknown, an absent checkout is declared unknown, and health claims are dated runs kept as evidence, not standing truths. ## The name A trellis is the lattice a garden grows against. Climbing plants grip a lattice at many points, not one, and the lattice holds because every point it promises to hold is checked. The family is a garden of contract modules, and its health is a multi-point question, never a single green badge. ## Status Version 0.8.0. The probe, grid, and verdict engine is `implemented` as a tested reference library. Family health statements live in `docs/evidence/` as dated observed runs. The engine covers the family's module repositories. The harness and design canon keep their own checks. ## Install ```bash npm install @vidoxlabs/trellis ``` Requires Node >= 22.13. Zero runtime dependencies. ## Modules | Module | What it holds | Label | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `point.mjs` | The four test points and the probe record: deterministic checks, fail closed, dedicated to one point. | `implemented` | | `score.mjs` | Verdict math: pass, fail, unknown; fail outranks unknown, unknown outranks pass, and nothing is ever silently passed. | `implemented` | | `grid.mjs` | The multi-point grid: run probes against injected subjects and roll the results up per subject and per point. | `implemented` | | `probes.mjs` | The default probe lists for each family member and the cross-family consistency probes. A claim a member made after its first release is probed from the version that made it; an older checkout reads unknown. | `implemented` | The bundle runner, `scripts/family.mjs` (`npm run family`), wires the grid to the canonical family workspace: it loads each sibling's modules, runs the default probes, runs each sibling's own test suite for the operational point, and prints the dated report the evidence docs record. ## The family The family follows one design law: ordinary botanical words for public products, mirroring five flower-named personas ([the law](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary/blob/main/docs/family.md)). | Name | Province | | :--- | :--- | | [`seed`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) | Harness foundation: runs, tools, providers | | [`capillary`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary) | Context retrieval and relations, provenance-first | | [`myosotis`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/myosotis) | Memory with consent and structural forget | | [`aestivation`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/aestivation) | Plans, verdicts, and the gate before assembly | | [`drosera`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/drosera) | Tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks | | `trellis` (this repo) | Multi-point testing with dated evidence | | [`bloom`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) | The team workspace harness | | [`docs`](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs) | Family documentation, synced from every public repository | The line grows against the trellis: the products are the plants; this is the lattice they are checked against. ## Documentation - `AGENTS.md`: start here before editing. Stay in this repository's province. - `docs/charter.md`: mission, principles, non-goals. - `docs/architecture.md`: probes, grid, verdicts; engine and bundle runner. - `docs/contracts/`: the probe and grid contracts. - `docs/interop.md`: what each sibling is probed on, and the boundaries. - `docs/evidence/`: dated observed family runs, with their receipts. ## Development ```bash npm test # engine and probe mechanics, no siblings required npm run family # the bundle runner over the canonical workspace layout ``` Tests use the Node built-in runner. Adding a probe means adding the test that holds it. ## License MIT The Vidoxlabs name and mark are trademarks of Vidoxlabs LLC. They are not covered by this repository's MIT license.
documents.sources/vivarium/README.md: # Vivarium Seven systems, one agent platform. Vivarium is a personal agent platform. A person raises an assistant with a character and a job, gives it memory they consent to keep, and works alongside it: it reads what they point it at, asks before it acts outside its bounds, and leaves a record of what it did. It runs on the person's own machine first, and every route it takes to a model, a file, or a service is one the person switched on. This repository is the umbrella, not the product. It pins the seven systems at exact commits, records what each one owns, and gives a code agent the context it needs to work in the family without guessing. No product code lives here: the code lives in the seven repositories, and this tree is the one snapshot that says which code that is. bloom is Vivarium's user interface; the other six systems are the parts behind it. ## The systems | System | Role | Layer | | --- | --- | --- | | [seed](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/seed) | Harness floor: run records, tool identity, provider adapters, the shared contracts | floor | | [capillary](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/capillary) | Context: bounded retrieval with sources attached, and relations | peer | | [myosotis](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/myosotis) | Memory: consent to keep, structural forget | peer | | [drosera](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/drosera) | Tools: tool faces, skills, hooks, cookbooks | peer | | [aestivation](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/aestivation) | Review and delegation: plans, verdicts, questions to the person, the assembly gate | peer | | [bloom](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/bloom) | User interface: the desktop and web app, first-run setup, the head agent; the only composer | composer | | [trellis](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/trellis) | Testing from outside the call path: shape, behavior, consistency, operational probes | outside | The floor holds the contracts. The four peers do not import each other; they meet at seed. bloom is the only composer: it is where a person raises an agent and where the parts are put together. trellis tests from outside the call path, so a failure in the tree is not a failure the tree can hide. ## System map ```mermaid flowchart BT bloom["bloom · interface"] capillary["capillary · context"] myosotis["myosotis · memory"] drosera["drosera · tools"] aestivation["aestivation · review"] trellis["trellis · probes"]:::outside seed["seed · harness floor"]:::floor bloom -->|imports drosera 7a396c0| drosera bloom -->|imports seed 0d158cd| seed bloom -.->|contracts| seed capillary -.->|contracts| seed myosotis -.->|contracts| seed drosera -.->|contracts| seed aestivation -.->|contracts| seed capillary -.->|"context to memory, planned"| myosotis trellis -.->|probes| bloom trellis -.->|probes| capillary trellis -.->|probes| myosotis trellis -.->|probes| drosera trellis -.->|probes| aestivation trellis -.->|probes| seed linkStyle 2,3,4,5,6,7 stroke-dasharray: 6 4 linkStyle 8,9,10,11,12,13 stroke-dasharray: 2 4 classDef floor stroke-width:3px classDef outside stroke-dasharray: 4 3 ``` Solid is an import today, labelled with the pinned short SHA. Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. `npm run check` is offline and deterministic. It fails when a generated file drifts from the pins, when a submodule is not at its gitlink, when a relative link or a `systems/` path does not resolve, or when a public-safety rule trips. `npm test` runs the unit tests for the tool itself. ## How changes flow 1. **Change a system in its own repository.** A pull request there, its own tests, its own review. Nothing in this repository edits a submodule. 2. **The pin moves here.** Either the scheduled bump opens a pull request with the new pins and the regenerated manifest and map, or a person runs `npm run sync` and opens `chore(systems): bump `. Either way the pin is a commit that is on that system's `main`. 3. **Readers get the prose from the docs hub.** [docs](https://github.com/Vidoxlabs/docs) syncs every system's README and documentation, so this repository links to those pages instead of copying them. 4. **`docs` is linked, not pinned.** It is product-neutral and may serve more than one product, so it is not part of the snapshot.
